site.name: vaultkey
site.summary: vaultkey-clone Fictional password manager "Vaultkey" — short marketing landing + main pricing page. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Short landing: hero with title / dual CTAs; faux app screenshot (categorized sidebar + searchable item list with passkey / family / 2FA tags); 7-name trust strip; 3 why-cards; bottom CTA | | `pricing.html` | Main page: yearly / monthly billing toggle (annual saves 20%); 3 plan cards (Personal $0 forever, Family $3.99/mo featured, Business per-seat); **Business per-seat slider 3–200 with linked number input**, 5-tier volume pricing (3–24 / 25–49 / 50–99 / 100–199 / 200+) with monthly + yearly totals; enterprise contact strip; 25-row grouped feature comparison table (5 groups: Vault & sync / Sharing / Security / Admin & compliance / Support); 8-question FAQ accordion | | `styles.css` | Brand color #1E1B4B indigo + #A3E635 lime accent; Inter + JetBrains Mono; responsive at 2 breakpoints (>1000 / <1000 / <640) |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full vaultkey system, prioritizing the primary settings/privacy flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The pricing flow is generally understandable and functional, but several high-value controls feel incomplete or misleading because they behave like placeholders or dead links. On mobile, the page also has a real responsiveness problem: horizontal overflow persists, tap targets are small, and the business seat input is unlabeled, reducing usability in the core pricing calculator. I did not fully validate every adjacent nav destination, so there may be additional inert links beyond the ones observed.

exploration_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore the Vaultkey marketing and pricing experience, with emphasis on the pricing calculator, plan comparison, FAQ behavior, and mobile usability of navigation and tap targets.
exploration_plan.summary: Start on the landing page to validate the primary conversion paths into pricing and any obvious navigation dead ends, then move into the pricing page as the core interaction surface. On pricing, exercise the billing toggle, all plan CTAs, the business seat control and linked number input across key ranges, the feature comparison table, and the FAQ accordion states. Repeat the critical checks in a mobile viewport to confirm responsive behavior and to capture the small tap-target warnings seen in prescan.
assumptions: The site is a static marketing clone with only two HTML pages and no hidden authenticated product flows.
Placeholder navigation items with href '#' may be inert or non-navigating; they should still be checked for feedback and accidental page changes.
The pricing page contains the highest-risk interactive logic because it includes multiple stateful controls and calculated pricing outputs.
FAQ entries are expected to be accordion-style even though the prescan only confirmed their presence, not their expanded state behavior.
risk_hotspots: pricing.html: yearly/monthly billing toggle and consistency of annual 20% savings messaging
pricing.html: Business seat slider (3–200) and linked number input synchronization
pricing.html: tiered volume pricing breakpoints and monthly/yearly total calculations
pricing.html: 8-question FAQ accordion open/close behavior and content accessibility
index.html: small mobile tap targets in the top navigation and primary CTA buttons
All pages: placeholder links for Security, Enterprise, Help, Sign in, and Download free

phases.title: Landing page conversion path
phases.objective: Validate the homepage’s main marketing flow and whether the primary calls to action lead cleanly to pricing or reveal broken/inert links.
key_checks: Click 'See plans →' from the hero and confirm it opens pricing.html
Click 'See pricing →' at the bottom and confirm it also opens pricing.html
Inspect whether 'Download free' and top-nav placeholder links are inert, return to page, or trigger any unexpected behavior
Check that the faux app screenshot remains visually coherent and does not overlap at the current viewport
exit_criteria: Both pricing CTAs have been exercised and their destinations verified
All visible homepage links have been clicked or intentionally classified as inert
No unexpected console or network errors appear during navigation

phases.title: Pricing page baseline structure
phases.objective: Confirm the pricing page layout, plan cards, and toggle state messaging before deeper interaction testing.
key_checks: Verify the default billing mode on load and the corresponding plan prices
Click the yearly/monthly toggle and confirm all visible plan prices update consistently
Check the three plan cards for clear differentiation, especially the featured Family plan
Click plan CTAs such as 'Get Personal', 'Start free 30-day trial', and 'Start 14-day trial' to confirm they are functional or clearly inert
exit_criteria: Default and alternate billing states have both been observed
Each plan card CTA has been exercised once
The featured plan treatment and pricing copy are captured without layout regressions

phases.title: Business calculator and pricing thresholds
phases.objective: Stress the interactive business pricing controls and validate state synchronization and breakpoint behavior.
key_checks: Move the Business seat slider to minimum, mid-range, and maximum values
Edit the linked number input and confirm it updates the slider and pricing output correctly
Verify tiered pricing changes at the published breakpoints (3–24, 25–49, 50–99, 100–199, 200+)
Check both monthly and yearly totals after toggling billing while the seat count is set to edge values
Confirm the enterprise contact strip remains visible and usable near the business section
exit_criteria: Slider and number input remain synchronized across tested ranges
At least one value from each pricing tier has been validated
Monthly and yearly outputs respond correctly to both seat changes and billing mode changes

phases.title: Comparison table and FAQ behavior
phases.objective: Validate information architecture and state changes in the feature comparison table and FAQ accordion.
key_checks: Scroll through the grouped feature comparison table and confirm section headings and row structure remain readable
Check for horizontal overflow or clipped cells in the comparison table at narrower widths
Expand several FAQ items, including the first, middle, and last questions, and then collapse them again
Verify only the intended FAQ item(s) open at a time if the control behaves like an accordion
exit_criteria: Comparison table content is readable across the tested viewport
Multiple FAQ items have been opened and closed successfully
No broken spacing, overlapping text, or inaccessible toggle states are observed

phases.title: Mobile responsive verification
phases.objective: Repeat the critical conversion and calculator checks on mobile to confirm responsive layout and tap-target usability.
key_checks: Recheck the homepage primary CTAs and top navigation at mobile width
Confirm the pricing page toggle, plan CTAs, and business controls remain operable on touch-sized viewports
Look for tap-target issues on the top nav and primary buttons flagged by prescan
Confirm the comparison table and FAQ do not become unusably cramped or overflow badly on mobile
exit_criteria: Critical homepage and pricing interactions have been repeated in mobile viewport
Any tap-target or overflow issues are documented with concrete affected controls
Mobile behavior is compared against desktop for the main pricing flow

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all known HTML pages: index.html and pricing.html.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise every visible CTA on the landing page, the billing toggle, all plan CTAs, the business seat slider and linked input, representative pricing breakpoints, several FAQ items, and the comparison table sections.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat the homepage conversion path and the pricing calculator/FAQ checks at mobile viewport, with special attention to the small tap-target warnings and any overflow in the pricing table.

notes: Prescan shows no console or network errors, so the run should focus on interaction fidelity, responsiveness, and content/state consistency rather than fault recovery.
Because the site is small, aim for near-exhaustive coverage of visible controls rather than broad browsing depth.

findings.user_goal: Open a meaningful sign-in or account path from the header
findings.problem: The mobile Sign in link behaves like a placeholder anchor instead of a real destination, changing only the URL to `#` with no page change or feedback.
findings.evidence: In the mobile viewport, clicking `index.html: Sign in` changed the URL from `index.html` to `index.html#`, and the observed href is `#`. The control is also very small at 44×16px.
findings.why_it_matters: Users expect a header sign-in action to take them to authentication. A dead-looking control creates distrust and makes the site feel unfinished.
findings.suggestion: Route Sign in to a real login page or modal, or relabel it as unavailable until implemented. Increase the tap target to a full-height header button.

findings.user_goal: Start the free download/trial from the homepage or pricing page
findings.problem: The prominent "Download free" CTA on the homepage appears inert, so a major conversion action does not produce a meaningful result.
findings.evidence: Clicking `index.html: Download free` caused no URL change and no visible-text change, and the control uses `href="#"` according to the trajectory notes.
findings.why_it_matters: When a primary CTA looks real but does nothing, users lose confidence and may abandon the flow, assuming the product or trial is not available.
findings.suggestion: Link the CTA to an actual download or signup step. If it is informational, change the label and styling so it does not promise an action it cannot complete.

findings.user_goal: Use the personal plan CTA to begin purchasing or signing up
findings.problem: The Personal plan CTA is visually primary but behaves like a placeholder, undermining the plan card’s main action.
findings.evidence: Clicking `pricing.html: Get Personal` produced no navigation or visible change in the earlier trajectory, and the control’s href is `#` in the discovered interactables.
findings.why_it_matters: A plan card CTA is one of the most important purchase affordances on the page; if it is inert, users cannot complete the conversion path and may question the legitimacy of the pricing page.
findings.suggestion: Connect the button to the purchase/signup flow or replace it with a disabled state and explanatory copy until the flow exists.

findings.user_goal: Use the pricing calculator comfortably on a phone
findings.problem: The mobile pricing page overflows horizontally, so the layout is not fully contained within the viewport.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings repeatedly report `Page width 395px exceeds viewport 390px`, and the final mobile observation still shows horizontal overflow while the pricing content is visible.
findings.why_it_matters: Horizontal overflow makes pricing cards and controls harder to scan and can hide or partially clip key values, especially near the calculator and CTA area.
findings.suggestion: Remove the extra 5px overflow by tightening widths, margins, or flex gaps around the pricing section and header.

findings.user_goal: Adjust team size precisely in the Business pricing calculator
findings.problem: The Business seat number input has no visible label, placeholder, or ARIA label, making it hard to discover and interpret.
findings.evidence: The layout warnings include `missing_input_label` for the number input, and the interactable is shown simply as an unlabeled input with current value `12`/later `50` seats.
findings.why_it_matters: Unlabeled inputs are especially problematic in a pricing calculator because users may not understand what the field does or how it relates to the slider and totals.
findings.suggestion: Add a persistent visible label such as "Team size" and an accessible name. Keep the input close to the slider with clear helper text.

findings.user_goal: Switch billing modes quickly on a phone
findings.problem: The yearly/monthly billing toggle is functional but too small for comfortable touch use, and it contributes to the page’s cramped mobile feel.
findings.evidence: The mobile viewport flags both tabs as below guidance: `Yearly · save 20%` is 153×32px and `Monthly` is 90×32px. The page also reports horizontal overflow while the toggle is in view.
findings.why_it_matters: Small tabs increase mis-taps and slow down a frequent pricing task, especially when users are comparing monthly versus yearly costs.
findings.suggestion: Increase the tab height to at least 44px and add more spacing/padding so the toggle feels easier to use on touch devices.

findings.user_goal: Navigate to real sections from the header
findings.problem: Several top navigation items behave like placeholders rather than meaningful destinations, which makes the header feel unreliable.
findings.evidence: Clicking `pricing.html: Security` changed the URL to a bare hash with no visible content change, and earlier notes also show `Product` and `Help` behaving similarly as self-link or hash placeholders.
findings.why_it_matters: Navigation should set correct expectations. Placeholder links in the main nav make the site feel unfinished and create doubt about whether the product is fully built.
findings.suggestion: Either wire these links to actual pages/sections or visually mark them as unavailable/development items so users do not expect real navigation.

findings.user_goal: Tap important header actions accurately on mobile
findings.problem: The header contains several undersized touch targets, increasing the chance of mis-taps on a phone.
findings.evidence: Mobile layout warnings flag `Sign in` at 44×16px, `Get Vaultkey` at 125×34px, and `Vaultkey` at 106×30px as below the 44px guidance.
findings.why_it_matters: Even if the targets are technically clickable, small hit areas create friction on mobile and make the primary navigation feel cramped.
findings.suggestion: Increase vertical padding and tap area for the header links, or consolidate them into a more mobile-friendly menu.

findings.user_goal: Understand whether CTA clicks did anything
findings.problem: Some CTA clicks only update the URL fragment to `#`, which is weak feedback for high-importance actions.
findings.evidence: The mobile `Start free 30-day trial` CTA changed the URL to `pricing.html#`, and the mobile `Sign in` link changed to `index.html#`. These are visible changes, but they do not communicate a real destination or state change.
findings.suggestion: Replace fragment-only placeholders with real destinations or richer feedback such as a dialog, page transition, or disabled state with explanation.
findings.source_hint: pricing.html CTA `Start free 30-day trial`; index.html `Sign in`

gaps: Only directly exercised 66% of visible interactive feature signatures.
42% of actions produced no visible URL/text change; this may indicate dead controls or repeated probes.
